hero.headline: Spis — interface references you can cite
hero.lede: An open corpus of {{record_count}} real-interface records across {{catalog_count}} families. Every record states its source, hashes, provenance class, and measured state, so the reference and its evidence travel together.
hero.metaDescription: Spis is an open, evidence-grade reference corpus: {{record_count}} records across {{catalog_count}} interface families, each with source, hashes, provenance class, and measured state.

sections.heading: A screenshot without provenance is a guess
sections.lede: Screenshot libraries show pictures of interfaces with no way to tell what was measured, where the media came from, or whether the numbers attached mean anything. When you quote a pattern, you cannot say what evidence stands behind it.

items.title: Unknown origin
items.text: Media with no recorded source and no hashes cannot be checked, updated, or trusted when a product changes.

items.title: Invented completeness
items.text: Libraries imply coverage they never measured; nothing tells you which parts were actually examined.

sections.heading: The index is generated, and it refuses to lie
sections.lede: Catalog pages are rendered from records by a generator that compares the index, the records, and the files on disk, and refuses to publish a disagreement.

artifact.caption: `spis generate-example-catalogs --check` over the generated index
lines: check passed: index matches records and files

sections.heading: Cite the pattern and its evidence together
sections.lede: Browse all {{catalog_count}} catalogs on GitHub, read the evidence contract every record meets, and take the whole corpus under Apache-2.0.
